title: Parabolic cusp criterion for holomorphic convexity of geometrically finite ball quotients
difficulty_reason: For the nontrivial implication the author decomposes the quotient into a relatively compact core and finitely many parabolic cusp pieces, combines a smoothed distance-to-convex-core function with local strictly plurisubharmonic cusp exhaustions, chooses a convex reparameterization to control the overlaps, and checks properness along both ideal boundary and cusps. The source also proves the horoball quotient equivalence needed for the converse. The author explicitly attributes the method of the core implication to Chen; all source-local construction and cited inputs remain identified.

readability.basis: Existing 22-page reader from batch-14872-14875-r004; physically viewed pages 2–3 containing all three theorem conditions and pages 16–17 containing the supporting lemma and complete proof.

dedup.scope: Current master title searches for geometrically finite, complex hyperbolic and holomorphic convex; same-work published version and arXiv alias inspected by their actual selected statements.

compared.relation: Same publication, selected Theorem 5 assumes critical exponent 2 and a compact positive-dimensional analytic subset and concludes complex Fuchsian rigidity. Theorem 4 instead characterizes holomorphic convexity by cusp quotients for geometrically finite torsion-free groups.

Earlier arXiv version of the same work, selected lemma lem-cvx-psh puts compact complex subvarieties of a Kähler manifold in the zero locus of a convex function. It is used as a supporting observation and does not state the cusp equivalence.

source_disclosures: The (2) to (3) construction is explicitly inspired by Chen’s proof of Theorem 1.4; no independent certification or uncredited novelty claim is made.
